content:
emily: hi team — emily here, first week on runtime. trying to build the python wheel from source on Ubuntu 20.04 with an RTX A5000. make/pip wheel fails at link with undefined refs to CUDA register symbols. anyone seen this?

todd: welcome! quick q: are you using the dev container or building inside a conda env on host? paste the exact linker error if you can.

emily: building on host in conda py3.10. error snippet: ```/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc -ccbin g++ -shared -o libinference.so ... /tmp/cc123.o: In function `__device_stub__Z4kernv': undefined reference to `__cudaRegisterFatBinary' collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status```

yun: that typically means the final link step isn't pulling in cudart (or toolchain mismatch). couple things we recommend for new hires: 1) pin host compiler to g++-9, 2) set CUDAHOSTCXX, 3) avoid mounting host CUDA into the container.

todd: concretely: sudo apt install gcc-9 g++-9 && sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-9 60. then export CUDAHOSTCXX=/usr/bin/g++-9 before running nvcc. Our CI uses gcc-9.

emily: i switched g++ to 9 and set CUDAHOSTCXX, still getting a slightly different link error (device stubs).

yun: try checking ld flags: if --as-needed is present the linker can drop cudart symbols. For python extension builds add -Wl,--no-as-needed or explicitly append -lcudart to the link libraries. Also confirm LD_LIBRARY_PATH includes $CUDA_HOME/lib64 and that /usr/local/cuda is the toolkit you expect.

emily: ldd on the built .so shows libcuda.so -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 which is fine (driver). i also noticed our setup.py wasn't passing library_dirs, so it relied on system search paths.

build-bot: FYI CI builds inside image redwood/runtime-dev:2026-03, with CUDA 12.1 and g++-9. See build log: https://ci.redwood-internal/runtime/5821 (last green).

todd: another subtle thing: mixed arch/gencode flags across modules cause unresolved device stubs. Make sure NVCCFLAGS are consistent (e.g., -gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86) for all CUDA compilation units. Also run a clean: rm -rf build/ dist/ *.so *.o.

emily: aha — i had built one of the extension objects earlier with sm_80 then recompiled others with sm_86. cleaned everything and re-ran with consistent -gencode flags. build progressed further.

yun: if you're still blocked, try building the shared lib with CMake directly (cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-9 -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.1) then pip wheel can consume the prebuilt .so. That avoids pip/build isolation oddities.

emily: that did it — building the .so separately with cmake then installing the wheel worked. unit tests starting. big thanks! :tada:

ops-bot: welcome emily — added onboarding task 'local wheel build' to your checklist.

emily: leaving a tiny note for future new hires: if wheel linking fails, check CUDAHOSTCXX + consistent arch flags + ld --no-as-needed before poking at cudart. saved me ~2 hours. :slightly_smiling_face:
